references.text: Jacob's dream of the ladder between heaven and earth, where God's angels went up and down ([ref:Gen 28:12|Genesis 28:12]). Jesus applies this image directly to himself as the Son of Man – he is the new "ladder of Jacob" that connects heaven and earth.

The broader context of Jacob's dream at Bethel ([ref:Gen 28:10-17|Genesis 28:10-17]), where Jacob sees heaven opened and angels going up and down, and calls the place "the house of God" and "the gate of heaven." Jesus identifies himself as the fulfillment of this vision.

Ezekiel sees heaven opened ([ref:Ezek 1:1|Ezekiel 1:1]) and receives a vision of God's glory. The motif of the open heaven in John 1:51 has parallels with prophetic visions where heaven is opened for divine revelation.

Isaiah prays that God would tear open the heavens and come down ([ref:Isa 64:1|Isaiah 64:1]). The open heaven in Jesus' words points to this prayer now being answered through the coming of the Son of Man.

Daniel's vision of "one like a son of man" who comes with the clouds of heaven and receives dominion ([ref:Dan 7:13-14|Daniel 7:13-14]). Jesus uses the title "Son of Man" for himself, linking it to this messianic figure.
At Jesus' baptism, heaven was opened, and God's Spirit descended like a dove ([ref:Matt 3:16-17|Matthew 3:16-17]). The motif of the open heaven over Jesus is a recurring sign of his divine identity.

Stephen sees heaven opened and the Son of Man standing at God's right hand ([ref:Acts 7:56|Acts 7:56]). This is a direct fulfillment of Jesus' promise in John 1:51 that people would see heaven opened over the Son of Man.

Jesus speaks of the Son of Man who descended from heaven and will be lifted up ([ref:John 3:13-14|John 3:13-14]). The angels' ascending and descending over the Son of Man point to him as the connection between heaven and earth.

Jesus says that the Father has given the Son of Man authority to execute judgment ([ref:John 5:27|John 5:27]). The title "Son of Man" used in John 1:51 is central to the entire Gospel of John's Christology.
John sees heaven opened, and Christ rides out as the faithful and true ([ref:Rev 19:11|Revelation 19:11]). The open heaven reveals Christ's glory, in line with the promise in John 1:51.

The conversation with Nathanael just before, where Jesus demonstrates his supernatural knowledge ([ref:John 1:47-50|John 1:47-50]). Jesus promises Nathanael that he will see something even greater than this – namely, the open heaven and angels over the Son of Man.
